dialog.body: Utilities Division, water and sewer billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?
Good morning, Tony. Good morning to you, and I hope your day is going well and your family is well also. [pause] Sorry, one moment.
No problem, take your time.
Yes, thank you. My name is Nilson Fortes. I am calling about a water bill, and I have a small problem with it, nothing terrible, but it is bothering me.
Okay, sure. Tell me what's going on.

So. I bought a house just last month. On Coggeshall Avenue, number 185. And the first bill came in the mail, and the name on it is not my name. It is the name of the man who sold me the house. The former owner.
Ah, okay. That happens a lot actually, right after a sale. The account stays in the old owner's name until somebody tells us about the change. Do you have the bill in front of you?
Yes, I have it here. [pause] Yes. It says the account number, and then the name, and then the amount. The amount is, ah, one hundred eighty-four dollars and some cents.
Okay. And what's the service address printed on it?
Wait, wait. Let me look. [pause] It says, ah, Tillinghast Road. Oh. No, that is not right. That is my other house.
Your other house?

Yes, forgive me. I have two properties. The one I have had for many years, and this new one. And the bills, they come in similar envelopes, and I opened the wrong one first. So this bill with the old owner's name, it is, hmm, let me see. [pause] The sheet says Coggeshall. Yes. And the Tillinghast one is in my own name. So I was holding two papers and I mixed them. I am sorry.
No worries, easy to do. So just to be clear, the Tillinghast bill is in your name and that one's fine, and the Coggeshall bill is the one with the former owner's name on it.

Yes, correct. That one. But here is what annoys me, Tony. The bill is for one hundred eighty-four dollars, and I only moved in on the fifteenth of December. How can I owe so much when I was there only three weeks? The house was empty before, and I think the water was off, or nearly.

Right. Well, the bill probably covers a billing period that started before you took the house. Our reads go by the meter, so the bill could include usage from the previous owner's time, plus the base charges for the whole period.
So I am paying for him. That is what you are saying.
Not necessarily. That's what I'd want to look at. If the closing date was in mid-December, the usage before that should be his, and a final read should have been done for the sale.
The closing was the fifteenth of December. I have the paper from the closing. Nobody told me about a final read.
Okay. Let me pull up the account. What's the account number on the bill?
One moment, please. [pause] It is, ah, four, four, one, seven, dash, zero, three.
Four four one seven, dash zero three. Hang on, let me type that in.
Of course. Take your time. I am only eating my breakfast, a little cereal, it is late for breakfast I know. [pause] Please excuse me.
No, you're fine. Okay, I've got it. So the account is still under the previous owner. The last reading on file is from the end of November, and the bill you have goes through the end of December.
So there was no reading on the fifteenth.
Doesn't look like it. It looks like the system estimated the split, or just billed the whole period to the account. I can't tell from here which one.
Mm. That is what I thought. And this seems not fair to me. I am the new owner and I get a bill with another man's name, for days I was not there. I would like it corrected.

Understood. Here's what has to happen. First, we need to get the account moved into your name, and we'll need the closing date. Second, somebody has to look at the period and split it at the closing date, so the old owner is responsible for his part and you for yours.
Yes. Yes, that is what I want. And I do not want to pay the full one hundred eighty-four.
I hear you. Don't pay it yet until we sort it out. Do you have a copy of the closing statement, or just the date?
I have the whole paper. The date is the fifteenth of December, twenty twenty-five. I can send it, or bring it.
Bringing it by City Hall is fine, or you could drop off a copy. Either way I'll note the account now. And the name of the seller, can you read it to me off the bill so I match it right?
Yes. It is, ah, Harlan. H, A, R, L, A, N. And the last name is Voss, V, O, S, S.
Got it, Harlan Voss. That matches what I'm seeing.
Good. And my name, it is Nilson, N, I, L, S, O, N. Fortes, F, O, R, T, E, S.

Nilson Fortes. Okay. Now, I want to be straight with you. I can start the name change, but the adjustment on the bill, that needs one of our billing folks to look at the meter history and decide how to split it. I can't say right now what the corrected number will be.
I understand. But I would like someone to call me back with the answer. I do not want to be calling and calling, you understand. I am a busy man, I have two houses now. [pause] Excuse me.
Sure, that's fair. I'll put in a callback request. What's the best number?
It is four, zero, one, five, five, five, zero, one, nine, five.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one nine five. This is a landline, right? Is somebody home to pick up during the day?
Yes, yes, this is the house phone, and I am here today. Tomorrow I am at work until the afternoon, so after four is better.
Okay, I'll note after four o'clock for tomorrow and after that, whenever they get to it. Probably within a couple of days, I'd think.
A couple of days is acceptable. But please, tell them it is about the Coggeshall account, not the Tillinghast one. The Tillinghast one is correct and I do not want them to change it by mistake.

Good point, I'll write that in. Coggeshall Avenue, 185, account four four one seven dash zero three, former owner Harlan Voss, new owner Nilson Fortes, closing December fifteenth. Tillinghast is separate and stays as is.
Perfect. You are very thorough, Tony. Thank you.
Just doing the job. One more thing, when you come by with the closing paper, ask at the window for the utilities counter, and they'll scan it into the account so you don't have to do it twice.
Yes, I will do this this week. Is it also needed to bring my identification?
A photo ID wouldn't hurt. Usually the closing statement is the main thing, though.
Good. And the next bill, it will come in my name, after this change?
Once the account's transferred, yes. This current one might still show his name since it's already been generated, but the next cycle should be yours.
I see. So I may get another with his name, and I should not be surprised.
Right, if it was already printed. Hold onto anything that comes and mention it when they call you back.
Okay. I will keep everything on the kitchen table, in one pile. Separate from Tillinghast. [pause] I learned my lesson this morning.
Good system. Anything else I can do for you today?
No, that is all. Thank you again, and God bless you and your family. Please have a good afternoon.
You too, Mr. Fortes. Somebody will call you tomorrow after four. Take care.
Goodbye, Tony, goodbye.
